import json, os, sys, math, statistics, textwrap, platform
from pathlib import Path

input_path = Path("/mnt/data/beb18221386c82f8baed31972ea4d87a-data.json")
with input_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    data = json.load(f)

print(json.dumps({
    "loaded": True,
    "schema_version": data.get("schema_version"),
    "figure_kind": data.get("figure_kind"),

}, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
# Inspect the complete input structure and values needed for computation/rendering.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import json, math, statistics, platform
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap, TwoSlopeNorm
from matplotlib.font_manager import FontProperties

# ---------- Independent numerical calculation ----------
values = data["values"]
variables = data["variables"]
n = len(values)
p = len(variables)

if not (2 <= p <= 10):
    raise ValueError("correlation_heatmap requires 2–10 variables")
if any(len(row) != p for row in values):
    raise ValueError("Every row must contain one value per variable")
if n < 2:
    raise ValueError("Pearson correlation requires at least two common observations")
if not all(math.isfinite(float(x)) for row in values for x in row):
    raise ValueError("All common observations must be finite")

columns = [[float(row[j]) for row in values] for j in range(p)]

def pearson_independent(x, y):
    if len(x) != len(y) or len(x) < 2:
        raise ValueError("Invalid paired observations")
    mx = statistics.mean(x)
    my = statistics.mean(y)
    dx = [v - mx for v in x]
    dy = [v - my for v in y]
    sxx = math.fsum(v*v for v in dx)
    syy = math.fsum(v*v for v in dy)
    if sxx == 0 or syy == 0:
        return None
    r = math.fsum(a*b for a, b in zip(dx, dy)) / math.sqrt(sxx * syy)
    # Clamp only tiny floating overshoot.
    if r > 1 and r < 1 + 1e-15:
        r = 1.0
    if r < -1 and r > -1 - 1e-15:
        r = -1.0
    return float(r) if math.isfinite(r) else None

method = data["correlation_method"]
if method != "pearson":
    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported method for this input: {method}")

matrix = []
for i in range(p):
    row = []
    for j in range(p):
        r = pearson_independent(columns[i], columns[j])
        row.append(r)
    matrix.append(row)

if any(v is None for row in matrix for v in row):
    raise ValueError("A finite correlation matrix cannot be computed for constant data")

# ---------- Font selection and verification ----------
font_path = "/usr/share/fonts/opentype/noto/NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc"
font_prop = FontProperties(fname=font_path)
font_name = font_prop.get_name()

# Recheck that every required character is covered by the selected font.
tt = TTFont(font_path, fontNumber=0, lazy=True)
selected_cmap = set()
for table in tt["cmap"].tables:
    selected_cmap.update(table.cmap.keys())
missing_chars = sorted({ch for ch in required_text if not ch.isspace() and ord(ch) not in selected_cmap})
if missing_chars:
    raise RuntimeError(f"Selected font lacks required glyphs: {missing_chars}")

# ---------- Exact output configuration ----------
style = data["plot_config"]["style"]
width_px = int(style["width"])
height_px = int(style["height"])
dpi = 300
font_size = float(style["font_size"])
if width_px * height_px > 20_000_000:
    raise ValueError("Requested canvas exceeds 20 million pixels")

plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": font_name,
    "font.size": font_size,
    "text.usetex": False,
    "axes.unicode_minus": True,
    "axes.formatter.use_mathtext": False,
    "figure.facecolor": "white",
    "axes.facecolor": "white",
    "savefig.facecolor": "white",
})

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(width_px / dpi, height_px / dpi), dpi=dpi, facecolor="white")
fig.canvas.draw()
renderer = fig.canvas.get_renderer()

def wrap_preserving_all_chars(text, max_px, prop, fontsize):
    """Insert only newline characters; preserve every supplied character in order."""
    lines, current = [], ""
    for ch in text:
        trial = current + ch
        w, _, _ = renderer.get_text_width_height_descent(trial, prop, ismath=False)
        # Renderer uses the FontProperties size, so construct it at requested size below.
        if current and w > max_px:
            lines.append(current)
            current = ch
        else:
            current = trial
    if current or not lines:
        lines.append(current)
    wrapped = "\n".join(lines)
    if wrapped.replace("\n", "") != text:
        raise RuntimeError("Text wrapping did not preserve the exact supplied text")
    return wrapped

text_prop = FontProperties(fname=font_path, size=font_size)
title_prop = FontProperties(fname=font_path, size=font_size + 3, weight="bold")
caption_prop = FontProperties(fname=font_path, size=font_size)

# Dedicated regions: title, data axes, axis labels, caption, abbreviations.
ax = fig.add_axes([0.18, 0.39, 0.52, 0.46])
cax = fig.add_axes([0.77, 0.45, 0.025, 0.34])

palette = data["presentation"]["color_scale"]["palette"]
cmap = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("supplied_diverging", palette, N=256)
cs = data["presentation"]["color_scale"]
norm = TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=float(cs["min"]), vcenter=float(cs["center"]), vmax=float(cs["max"]))

arr = np.array(matrix, dtype=float)
im = ax.imshow(arr, cmap=cmap, norm=norm, aspect="equal", interpolation="nearest")

var_labels = []
for v in variables:
    unit = v.get("unit", "")
    var_labels.append(v["name"] if unit == "" else f'{v["name"]} ({unit})')

ax.set_xticks(range(p), labels=var_labels, fontproperties=text_prop)
ax.set_yticks(range(p), labels=var_labels, fontproperties=text_prop)
ax.tick_params(axis="both", length=0, pad=7)
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, p - 0.5)
ax.set_ylim(p - 0.5, -0.5)

# Cell borders.
ax.set_xticks(np.arange(-0.5, p, 1), minor=True)
ax.set_yticks(np.arange(-0.5, p, 1), minor=True)
ax.grid(which="minor", color="white", linewidth=2)
ax.tick_params(which="minor", bottom=False, left=False)

# Coefficients and common n in every cell.
annotation_texts = []
for i in range(p):
    for j in range(p):
        r = matrix[i][j]
        rgba = cmap(norm(r))
        luminance = 0.2126 * rgba[0] + 0.7152 * rgba[1] + 0.0722 * rgba[2]
        color = "black" if luminance > 0.58 else "white"
        t = ax.text(
            j, i, f"{r:.2f}\nn = {n}",
            ha="center", va="center", color=color,
            fontproperties=text_prop, linespacing=1.25
        )
        annotation_texts.append(t)

x_axis = data["presentation"]["axes"]["x"]
y_axis = data["presentation"]["axes"]["y"]
x_axis_label = x_axis["label"] if x_axis.get("unit", "") == "" else f'{x_axis["label"]} ({x_axis["unit"]})'
y_axis_label = y_axis["label"] if y_axis.get("unit", "") == "" else f'{y_axis["label"]} ({y_axis["unit"]})'
ax.set_xlabel(x_axis_label, fontproperties=text_prop, labelpad=12)
ax.set_ylabel(y_axis_label, fontproperties=text_prop, labelpad=14)

title_text = fig.text(
    0.5, 0.94, data["labels"]["title"],
    ha="center", va="center", fontproperties=title_prop
)

cb = fig.colorbar(im, cax=cax, ticks=cs["ticks"])
cb.ax.tick_params(labelsize=font_size, pad=6)
for lab in cb.ax.get_yticklabels():
    lab.set_fontproperties(text_prop)
cb.set_label(cs["label"], fontproperties=text_prop, labelpad=12)
cb.outline.set_linewidth(0.8)

caption = data["labels"]["caption"]
abbr_text = "；".join(
    f'{item["term"]}：{item["definition"]}'
    for item in data["presentation"]["abbreviations"]
)

caption_wrapped = wrap_preserving_all_chars(caption, width_px * 0.88, caption_prop, font_size)
abbr_wrapped = wrap_preserving_all_chars(abbr_text, width_px * 0.88, caption_prop, font_size)

caption_artist = fig.text(
    0.06, 0.245, caption_wrapped,
    ha="left", va="top", fontproperties=caption_prop, linespacing=1.25
)
abbr_artist = fig.text(
    0.06, 0.055, abbr_wrapped,
    ha="left", va="bottom", fontproperties=caption_prop, linespacing=1.25
)

# Draw final canvas and inspect required text bounding boxes.
fig.canvas.draw()
renderer = fig.canvas.get_renderer()
canvas_box = fig.bbox

required_artists = [
    ("title", title_text),
    ("x_axis_label", ax.xaxis.label),
    ("y_axis_label", ax.yaxis.label),
    ("caption", caption_artist),
    ("abbreviations", abbr_artist),
    ("colorbar_label", cb.ax.yaxis.label),
]
for idx, lab in enumerate(ax.get_xticklabels()):
    required_artists.append((f"x_tick_{idx}", lab))
for idx, lab in enumerate(ax.get_yticklabels()):
    required_artists.append((f"y_tick_{idx}", lab))
required_artists.extend((f"cell_{i}", t) for i, t in enumerate(annotation_texts))

bbox_report = {}
for name, artist in required_artists:
    bb = artist.get_window_extent(renderer=renderer)
    inside = (
        bb.x0 >= canvas_box.x0 - 1 and bb.y0 >= canvas_box.y0 - 1 and
        bb.x1 <= canvas_box.x1 + 1 and bb.y1 <= canvas_box.y1 + 1
    )
    bbox_report[name] = {
        "inside": inside,
        "bounds": [round(v, 1) for v in bb.bounds]
    }
    if not inside:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Required text is clipped or outside canvas: {name} {bb.bounds}")

# Specific non-overlap checks among dedicated regions.
def overlaps(a, b, pad=0):
    return not (
        a.x1 + pad <= b.x0 or b.x1 + pad <= a.x0 or
        a.y1 + pad <= b.y0 or b.y1 + pad <= a.y0
    )

xlab_bb = ax.xaxis.label.get_window_extent(renderer)
cap_bb = caption_artist.get_window_extent(renderer)
abbr_bb = abbr_artist.get_window_extent(renderer)
title_bb = title_text.get_window_extent(renderer)
axes_bb = ax.get_window_extent(renderer)

if overlaps(xlab_bb, cap_bb, pad=8):
    raise RuntimeError("X-axis label overlaps the caption region")
if overlaps(cap_bb, abbr_bb, pad=8):
    raise RuntimeError("Caption overlaps abbreviations")
if title_bb.y0 <= axes_bb.y1 + 8:
    raise RuntimeError("Title is too close to or overlaps the data axes")

# Save exact-sized PNG without cropping.
figure_path = Path("/mnt/data/figure.png")
fig.savefig(figure_path, dpi=dpi, facecolor="white", bbox_inches=None, pad_inches=0)
plt.close(fig)

with Image.open(figure_path) as img:
    actual_size = img.size
    if actual_size != (width_px, height_px):
        raise RuntimeError(f"PNG dimensions {actual_size} do not match requested {(width_px, height_px)}")

# ---------- Strict finite result JSON ----------
result = {
    "schema_version": 5,
    "figure_kind": data["figure_kind"],
    "language": data["language"],
    "title": data["labels"]["title"],
    "x_label": data["labels"]["x_label"],
    "y_label": data["labels"]["y_label"],
    "caption": data["labels"]["caption"],
    "plot_config": data["plot_config"],
    "correlation_method": data["correlation_method"],
    "mode": data["mode"],
    "variables": data["variables"],
    "statistics": {
        "n": n,
        "matrix": matrix
    },
    "legacy_contract": data["legacy_contract"],
    "presentation": data["presentation"],
    "environment": {
        "python_version": platform.python_version(),
        "matplotlib_version": matplotlib.__version__,
        "font": font_name
    }
}

result_path = Path("/mnt/data/result.json")
with result_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    json.dump(result, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, allow_nan=False)

print(json.dumps({
    "figure_path": str(figure_path),
    "result_path": str(result_path),
    "png_size": actual_size,
    "font": font_name,
    "n": n,
    "matrix": matrix,
    "caption_lines": caption_wrapped.count("\n") + 1,
    "abbreviation_lines": abbr_wrapped.count("\n") + 1,
    "layout_checks_passed": True
}, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
from PIL import Image
img=Image.open('/mnt/data/figure.png')
display(img.resize((1200,800)))
